gemini.notes: agy --dangerously-skip-permissions --print, model 'Gemini 3.8 Flash (High)'. Bundle read from disk via agy tools. BUMPED 3.6 -> 3.8 on 2026-09-05 at the operator's request, verified the same day from `agy models`. PRICING CORRECTED 2026-09-06 from $0.3/$1.2 to $1.5/$7.5 per Mtok. The old figure was NOT a 3.8 rate and was not a 3.6 rate either: $0.3/$1.2 is exactly this registry's own `gemini-api` entry for gemini-2.5-flash, so it was a carry-over from the 2.5 Flash REST rate that survived two model bumps. SOURCES, both dated 2026-09-06 and mutually independent: (1) the model-routing table embedded in the cmdc CLI 1.50.0 bundle (dist/cli.mjs), which prices google/gemini-3.8-flash via vertex at promptCost 1.5 / completionCost 7.5 / cacheReadCost 0.15, identically to 3.7 and 3.6; (2) https://commandcode.ai/docs/plans/goat, which publishes Gemini 3.8 Flash at $1.50 input / $7.50 output per Mtok. WHY THAT SOURCE IS TRUSTED HERE: the same cmdc table was checked against seven registry entries whose prices were obtained independently, and matched all seven exactly -- deepseek-flash 0.14/0.28, deepseek-http 1.74/3.48, muse-spark 0.1/0.2 (cache read 0.002, agreeing to three decimals with the `opencode models --verbose` figure recorded in that preset), longcat 0/0, minimax-http 0.3/1.2, kimi-http 0.95/4.0, glm-http 1.4/4.4. It disagreed with exactly one entry: this one, the entry whose own notes already declared itself unmeasured. WHAT THIS NUMBER IS AND IS NOT: it is the LIST RATE FOR THE MODEL as published by a gateway that resells it, and it is NOT a measurement of what Antigravity bills for this seat. agy runs on a subscription and exposes no per-token cost at all -- measured 2026-09-06 on agy 1.1.27, `agy session stats`, `agy config list` and `agy stats` all return 'unexpected argument' (a bogus subcommand returns the same, so the probe was checked against a control), and tools/token-truth.py still has no agy reader. So this seat's cost remains ESTIMATED, not reconciled; the change is that the estimate now uses the right model's list rate instead of a different model's. UNVERIFIED THIRD-PARTY CLAIM, recorded for the record and NOT relied on: an LLM answer relayed by the operator on 2026-09-06 put Antigravity's real rates at ~$0.75-1.50/M input and ~$3.75-9.00/M output. Nothing here confirms that claim; note only that the two measured sources above ($1.50/$7.50) fall inside the range it gives. The 3.6 entry below is kept and still selectable by -Model. NOTE 3.5 IS GONE from `agy models` as of the 2026-09-05 check, which makes the `gemini-flash-35` preset the same dead-preset shape ox-alpha was.

deepseek-v4-pro._variants_note: ⛔ 'low' and 'medium' REMOVED 2026-09-04. opencode declares high/max for this model and nothing else. Both were INERT -- era's preference loop is @(xhigh,max,high,medium,low) and stops at 'max', which IS declared -- so nothing era sent ever changed. They are gone anyway because an entry that lists a name opencode does not declare is a loaded gun: reorder the preference loop, or have opencode drop 'max' from this model, and era starts silently asking for a variant that is ignored, which is the exact 2026-08-26 muse-spark failure. There is no runtime signal for it; the guard is tests/OpencodeVariantDeclared.Tests.ps1.

deepseek-v4-flash._variants_note: ⛔ 'max' REMOVED 2026-09-04, and 'medium' with it because opencode never declared it. DIAGNOSED FROM opencode.db, not guessed: under --variant max this model reasons until it hits a 32,000-token OUTPUT ceiling and returns a message whose parts are {step-start, reasoning, step-finish} with NO text part -- so opencode prints nothing to stdout and exits 0, and era sees a clean exit with an empty capture. Two messages in the local opencode.db have output=32000 EXACTLY, and BOTH have 0 text chars; a SUCCESSFUL run on the same bundle came in at 31,942 output tokens, 58 short of failing. deepseek folds reasoning into the output count (its 'reasoning' field reads 0 while output is tens of thousands, unlike muse-spark which reports ~11k separately), so maximum effort can spend the entire ceiling before a single answer token is written. This model's useful answers are ~3k tokens. ⚠ THE BENEFIT IS UNPROVEN. The single validation run at 'high' was INCONCLUSIVE: era's own stall detector tree-killed it at 620.94s of no output growth, so it says nothing about whether 'high' avoids the ceiling. ✅ CORRECTED 2026-09-04: this note used to add 'while the model was still generating'. IT WAS NOT. Re-read from opencode.db, that turn (msg_06ba0f905001C6IJETWbMVPtzs) holds {step-start, reasoning(text="", no time.end), step-start, reasoning(text="", no time.end)} -- two empty reasoning parts 352s apart, 0 output tokens, never completed. A turn that IS generating writes into the reasoning part incrementally, and A TURN KILLED MID-GENERATION KEEPS WHAT IT HAD -- five never-completed turns in the same database still hold 2,999 to 105,568 characters of partial reasoning. This one kept zero across 633s and two step boundaries, while the sibling run six minutes earlier wrote 114,762 characters in 457.3s. The kill was correct; what the run was doing was the already-diagnosed zero-output failure, not work. What survives is the correlation above, not a demonstrated cure: this is a reasonable change on token-accounting evidence, and it should not be described as a fix until a run at 'high' is observed finishing on its own. 'high' IS declared by opencode for this model. THE 'costs nothing in stall budget' CLAIM THIS NOTE USED TO MAKE WAS WRONG on the half it waved through. It was true for a big bundle (620.94s either way at 124,188 bytes, because the overlay dominated) and false for a small one, where it called the 600s -> 300s drop 'still generous': measured across 655 productive deepseek-v4-flash turns in opencode.db, 26 of them (3.97%) went silent for longer than 300s, up to 570.2s. So on a small bundle that change would have killed roughly one productive round in twenty-five. Moot since 2026-09-04: Resolve-OpencodeStallPlan no longer derives the threshold from the variant name at all -- see docs/assessments/2026-09-04-stall-threshold-measured.md.

muse-spark-1.2-contributor.note: ⭐ SAME RULE AS ox-alpha-free BELOW: the `variants` list is what sets the stall threshold, and without an entry here era resolves variant='default' (120s stall base) and kills a reasoning model mid-think having captured only its banner. muse-spark is reasoning-capable with a 1,048,576-token context, so it will absolutely think longer than 120s on a real bundle. `--variant max` verified accepted 2026-08-26 by running `opencode run -m opencode-go/muse-spark-1.2-contributor --variant max` directly, which printed its `> build · muse-spark-1.2-contributor` banner and then the expected answer. Added at the same time as the preset, because a preset without this entry is a reviewer that cannot review. THE `--variant max` VERIFICATION ABOVE IS LEFT STANDING AS THE RECORD AND IS WORTHLESS AS EVIDENCE: acceptance proves nothing, because opencode does not validate variant names at all (`--variant totally-bogus-zzz` is accepted too, measured 2026-09-04). This model declares minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh and has no 'max', so what that check confirmed was a no-op. Corrected to `xhigh` on 2026-09-04. SUPERSEDED in the default panel by 1.3 on 2026-09-04, and KEPT rather than deleted: 1.2 is still active, `-Model` is used verbatim by the adapter, and without this entry an explicit pin to 1.2 would fall back to variant='default' and its 120s stall base. ✅ SUPERSEDED IN PART, 2026-09-04: the `variants` list NO LONGER SETS THE STALL THRESHOLD. Resolve-OpencodeStallPlan stopped deriving anything from the variant name that day -- measured, the name predicts nothing about how long a run stays silent, and the 120s 'default' tier this note warns about was killing 8.07% of productive era-seat turns (docs/assessments/2026-09-04-stall-threshold-measured.md). So a missing entry here is no longer fatal. IT STILL DECIDES WHAT era SENDS: with no entry the resolver returns 'default' and no --variant flag is passed at all, so the seat runs at opencode's own reasoning effort. Keep the entry; the consequence of losing it is now a quieter seat rather than a killed one.

muse-spark-1.3-contributor.note: ⭐ SAME RULE AS 1.2 ABOVE AND ox-alpha-free BELOW: the `variants` list is what sets era's OWN stall threshold, and without an entry here era resolves variant='default' (120s stall base) and kills a reasoning model mid-think having captured only its banner. Added 2026-09-04 with the 1.2 -> 1.3 default bump. `--variant max` verified accepted that day by running `opencode run -m opencode-go/muse-spark-1.3-contributor --variant max` directly. Also verified the same day: era does NOT pass `--variant default` -- backends/opencode.ps1 omits the flag entirely when the resolved variant is 'default' -- so this list is the only thing that makes the flag appear at all. (`--variant default` IS accepted by opencode if passed; era simply does not pass it.) ✅ RESOLVED THE SAME DAY, AND THE VALUE ABOVE CHANGED AS A RESULT. This entry said `max` for one commit, copied from 1.2. `opencode models --verbose` declares this model's variants as minimal / low / medium / high / xhigh -- THERE IS NO `max`. And OPENCODE DOES NOT VALIDATE VARIANT NAMES: measured, `--variant totally-bogus-zzz` returns exit 0 and a normal answer, identical in shape to `--variant max`. So the undeclared name was being silently IGNORED and this seat ran at opencode's DEFAULT reasoning effort while era believed it had asked for maximum -- from 2026-08-26, when muse-spark entered the default panel, to 2026-09-04. Now `xhigh`, which the model actually declares. THE REGISTRY HALF COULD NOT BE CHANGED ALONE: era's preference loop is @('xhigh','max','high','medium','low') and had to learn 'xhigh' in the same commit, or it would match nothing here, fall back to variant='default', and hand a reasoning model the 120s stall base -- turning a silent no-op into the ox-alpha kill. Resolve-OpencodeStallPlan gives 'xhigh' and 'max' the same 600s budget on purpose: they are two providers' names for "think as long as you like", not two tiers. Guarded by tests/OpencodeVariantDeclared.Tests.ps1 against tests/fixtures/opencode-declared-variants.json, a dated snapshot of what opencode declares. ✅ SUPERSEDED IN PART, 2026-09-04: the `variants` list NO LONGER SETS THE STALL THRESHOLD. Resolve-OpencodeStallPlan stopped deriving anything from the variant name that day -- measured, the name predicts nothing about how long a run stays silent, and the 120s 'default' tier this note warns about was killing 8.07% of productive era-seat turns (docs/assessments/2026-09-04-stall-threshold-measured.md). So a missing entry here is no longer fatal. IT STILL DECIDES WHAT era SENDS: with no entry the resolver returns 'default' and no --variant flag is passed at all, so the seat runs at opencode's own reasoning effort. Keep the entry; the consequence of losing it is now a quieter seat rather than a killed one.

muse-spark-tmux.notes: muse-spark over the tmux TUI transport (backends/tmux.ps1). OPT-IN ONLY: not in config/defaults.json, so a bare /era never selects it. Paired with the `muse-spark` preset for A/B -- same model, same pricing, different transport. ⚠ THE TUI HAS NO --variant FLAG (measured 2026-09-06: present on `opencode run`, absent on the TUI), so this seat runs at opencode's DEFAULT reasoning effort while `muse-spark` sends --variant xhigh. Measured across 7 tmux runs, reasoning tokens were 2,799-8,608 against a single process-spawn observation of 9,221 -- the run-to-run spread is wide enough that no effort difference is demonstrated, and none is ruled out. A project opencode.json variant key was tried and showed no reliable effect (one run above the no-config range, one below). Treat the effort setting as UNPROVEN, not as equivalent. `--pure` was added and then removed: it stopped the operator's tmux-bell plugin signalling into era's socket, but on the plugin-set axis rather than the environment one, and it would also disable the turn-end plugin the design wants era to ship. The signal problem is now handled in backends/tmux.ps1's teardown, which pauses between kill-window and kill-server so a dying seat's last hooks land on a LIVE socket. NOTE 2026-09-06: the sibling `longcat-tmux` preset was DELETED the day it was added. cmdc gained a process-spawn backend (backends/cmdc.ps1) hours later, which reaches the same model with no server, no windows, no watchdog and no cross-session blast radius -- so carrying the same model over this transport as well was strictly worse and only invited someone to pick the wrong one.
